title: Plan K netns RCA: daemon lifecycle race + seccomp separation; verdict = workflow-only, no formal R&D
body: Deep RCA (read-only) of recurring GitHub Actions Docker netns roadblocks in Plan K (R10/R11/R15/R16/R17). VERDICT: no architectural/topology change required; workflow-design refinement only (plan amendment), no formal R&D. FACTS: (1) The `bind-mount /proc/<pid>/ns/net -> /var/run/docker/netns/<id>: no such file or directory` error is a Docker daemon libnetwork/osl namespace-lifecycle race (moby/moby#50750, containerd/containerd#12141, langgenius/dify#7739 ordinary compose-up, moby/moby#46490) — moby >=28.0 removed the OCI prestart hook and sets up networking between containerd task create and start using the returned pid; if /proc/<pid>/ns/net vanishes in that window, the bind-mount fails. Identical error reproduced by unrelated projects; compose uses default bridge; error occurs before any app code → NOT an app defect. (2) Trigger amplifier: ~10 containers started simultaneously (up -d full stack) widens the race window; two-phase bring-up (db+migrate+admin, then rest) already reduces it. (3) R15's `up exits 0 while services stay Created` proves daemon-side start-abort isn't propagated as a pipeline failure → the committed post-up state reconciliation (2d84d07, ps -a fix b3e3127/e6b5c3f) is the correct fail-closed deterministic gate. (4) SEPARATION: R16/R17 sandbox-runner EPERM (statx/fsmount; getcwd/vfork) is a DIFFERENT root cause — the custom seccomp profile couldn't host the full worker/bwrap; fixed by P3-S3 amendment → moby v28.0.0 default allowlist (414) + pivot_root (415), committed e6b5c3f, pushed to R18 33228898244. Residual risk: bwrap --unshare-all inside a cap_drop ALL container on Ubuntu 24.04 may still hit AppArmor userns restrictions; if R18 fails on sandbox, that is a seccomp/security-posture design question (bounded options: apparmor=unconfined/seccomp unconfined for sandbox-runner, or documented honest gated OS-isolation with SubprocessSandboxRunner containment), NOT a topology change and NOT a reason to skip sandbox. STALE ARTIFACTS found: HATCHET_LIVE_VALIDATION_HANDOFF.md §6 defect report (lines 184-210) still describes the 3 live tests as RecordingClient/executor=None — already repaired in-tree (support-researcher L5, plan P3-S4 note); handoff §1 still shows top-level denied image in hatchet.py while actual HATCHET_SERVER_IMAGE (hatchet.py:61) is the sub-path engine image (fixed P2-S2). RECOMMENDED amendments to Plan K (all within approved DD CI stream): (a) daemon health preflight (docker info + version assert) before up; (b) serialized startup batches (db → migrate+admin → engine+dashboard → api+worker+sandbox-runner) to narrow the netns race window; (c) keep bounded retry + reconciliation fail-closed; (d) per-service start/retry only if reconciliation shows recurrence; (e) do NOT use `--wait` as sole gate (one-shots exit; --wait needs healthchecks); (f) runner capability assertions (docker version >= 28, kernel, disk) as diagnostics. All preserve real callbacks/hosted evidence/no skips/no second scheduler.

title: Netns repair research: R16 daemon race vs R17 workflow-induced absence
body: Research for the netns repair DD. Findings: (1) R16 (33228084721/job 99035605497) had the TRUE daemon netns race signature `Error response from daemon: bind-mount /proc/<pid>/ns/net -> /var/run/docker/netns/<id>: no such file or directory` during compose up, PLUS three real defects per exec-manager L103: worker gRPC TLS WRONG_VERSION_NUMBER (SDK default tls strategy vs plaintext engine), reconcile `docker compose ps -q` (no -a) hiding exited one-shots -> migrate/admin always absent, sandbox seccomp bwrap EPERM. (2) R17 (33228376245/job 99036443345) had NO daemon netns error; startup fully succeeded (preflight, db healthy, migrate/admin Exited(0), JWT minted, worker registered C6 line); reconcile failed on sandbox-runner=restarting (getcwd/vfork EPERM) + migrate/admin=absent (ps -q excluding exited; fixed in e6b5c3f via ps -a -q). (3) sandbox-runner is profile-gated optional (compose.yaml:223-251) yet workflow forces --profile sandbox AND requires it running (validation.yml:328,347) — optional service conflated with mandatory gate; sandbox also lacks UMD_HATCHET_TOKEN/URL so even after seccomp fix its worker command exits 2 and restart: unless-stopped crash-loops. (4) Authoritative compose semantics: ps shows running only; -a includes stopped (and run-created one-offs); run --rm removes container and overrides restart policy; up rebuilds/recreates/starts; targeting profiled service by name activates its profile; State.Status enum created/running/restarting/exited/dead; Restarting bool + RestartCount + ExitCode via inspect. (5) Reconcile currently blind-retries up --no-build 5x on any missing state (validation.yml:346-384) — must instead classify created (transient, re-run up) vs restarting/exited-fail (capture logs/exit codes, fail) vs absent one-shots (verify ExitCode==0). Recommendation: keep mandatory set db/api/worker/hatchet-engine/hatchet-dashboard running + migrate/admin exited(0); sandbox-runner out of required_running; narrow transient marker to the exact bind-mount /proc/.../ns/net signature; observable diagnostics (docker inspect ExitCode/RestartCount/State.Error + log tails) before any retry. Sources: validation.yml:248-384, compose.yaml:37-288, exec-manager L96-L104, support-debugger L4, plan K P3-S3 notes, git commits 87b9a96/2d84d07/b3e3127/e6b5c3f, docker/compose + docker/docs Context7.

title: L9: run 33229130339 live-suite timeout — handler invocation contract mismatch (SDK 1.38.1)
body:
Run 33229130339/job 99038602321 (commit 6614b32): docker-e2e topology + readiness + external HTTP PASSED; live suite (tests/test_hatchet_live.py -m "cluster or docker") TIMED OUT with `stage_run rows=0, StageCompleted=0` — after the 6614b32 fixes (worker-extra install + on_conflict seed) let the 4 live tests actually submit for the first time.

PRIMARY ROOT CAUSE (verified against pinned SDK source @ tag py/1.38.1 + in-repo code):
SDK 1.38.1 invokes a task handler registered via `hatchet.task(name=...)(fn)` as `fn(workflow_input, ctx)` — TWO positional args (Task.call/aio_call in sdks/python/hatchet_sdk/runnables/task.py; Runner.run(action) path). UMD's `_make_handler` (src/umd/jobs/hatchet.py:229) returns `def handler(payload)` — ONE param, body `payload["input"]["manifest"]` (v0-style full-payload contract). EVERY dispatch raises `TypeError: handler() takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given`; retries=0 → task FAILED instantly → zero stage_run rows. Even with arity fixed, `payload["input"]` would KeyError (v1 passes the run input dict `{job_id,source_id,dag_universe,stage,manifest}` directly, no "input" wrapper).

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT: hermetic tests invoke the callback as `cb({"input": {"manifest": ...}})` (test_hatchet_live.py:464) — recording client passes the FULL v0 payload — so local/hermetic tests encode the same wrong contract and pass. L5's "unproven live execution: run_workflow payload shape" flag is exactly this.

RULED OUT as causal: host test installation (worker extra install landed, SDK imported, submissions ran); real JWT (run_workflow sync gRPC succeeded → engine validated token); network endpoint (host→127.0.0.1:7070 worked; worker→hatchet-engine:7070 works per R17's "waiting for tasks"); test/worker DB mismatch (live_db = shared compose umd DB via published 5432; P4-S7 single source of truth).

VERIFIED SDK SEMANTICS (1.38.1): Hatchet.worker(name, workflows=...) valid kwarg, type-checks BaseWorkflow (Standalone passes); Worker.start() → register_workflows() → admin.put_workflow (v1 gRPC) with sys.exit(1) on exception (crash-loop if TLS/auth fails — R16 pattern, but TLS now insecure + proven OK in R17); MinEngineVersion.SLOT_CONFIG=v0.78.23 < v0.105.2 → no legacy fallback; RunsClient.admin_client is a PROPERTY returning AdminClient; AdminClient.run_workflow is SYNC (v0 TriggerWorkflow gRPC, raises on grpc errors); ClientConfig reads HATCHET_CLIENT_TLS_STRATEGY + HATCHET_CLIENT_HOST_PORT env; token must be "ey" JWT.

LATENT GAPS for R&D: (1) cli.py ready-line count `len(handle.registered_workflows) or len(work_registry)` can print 9 with an EMPTY registered list (factory.start swallows registration exceptions via contextlib.suppress(Exception)); wait-for-worker.sh greps the line, not the engine — readiness can be fabricated; (2) test_live_hatchet_engine_visible_registration asserts LOCAL registration only (factory.start never contacts the engine; the test never calls worker.start()) — not engine-visible; (3) handler must be converted to v1 contract: `def handler(input, ctx)` reading `input["manifest"]` (or a compat shim) AND hermetic _invoke_callback updated to the same contract, else hermetic/live diverge again.

CONFIRMATION STEPS (need run 33229130339 artifacts: live-tests.log, diag-before/diag-final worker+engine logs): engine task runs should show FAILED with the TypeError for each umd-<stage>; worker log should show dispatch attempts, NOT a crash loop.

title: UMD orchestration architecture: sole-owner matrix, 9-task Hatchet translation, Postgres-gap analysis
body:
Full adversarial architecture review research on UMD orchestration. Key findings:

OWNERSHIP MATRIX (sole owner per concern, code-derived):
- DAG topology: src/umd/jobs/dag.py:30-78 STAGE_ORDER (9) / STAGE_DEPENDENCIES (11 edges) / STAGE_DEPENDENTS — sole lineage source, scheduler-agnostic, consumed by runner + invalidation planner.
- Dependency eligibility: dag.py + InvalidationPlanner (jobs/invalidation.py:75-128, pure descendant BFS) + JobService.rerun_stage/rerun_source/invalidate (application/jobs.py:205-321) + fail-closed canonical_evidence_refs (storage/postgres/job_repository.py:204-289, MissingRequiredEvidenceError/AmbiguousRequiredEvidenceError).
- Scheduling/dispatch: Hatchet SOLE v1 scheduler. ProductionDAGRunner/HatchetRunner.submit_workflow_runs (jobs/runner.py:202-257) submits ONE native workflow run per job; _build_native_workflow (jobs/hatchet.py:363-380) registers one workflow "umd-decomposition" with 9 durable_task(parents=STAGE_DEPENDENCIES) — engine v0.105.2 match-condition barrier (children not inserted until parents complete, verified prior research L14/L15).
- Claim: StageRunRepository.claim (storage/postgres/stage_repository.py:98-156) UNIQUE(idempotency_key) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; claim-before-side-effect.
- Idempotency/generation: StageManifest.idempotency_material (jobs/manifest.py:167-194) — universe+stage+source+segment+evidence_refs+input+schema+tools+config; job_id EXCLUDED; rerun_causation folded into input_manifest => fresh key for invalidated descendants; dag_universe folded in => no cross-universe aliasing.
- Retry: DurableStageExecutor.run in-process bounded exponential backoff (jobs/stage_execution.py:204-269, RetryPolicy max_attempts=3).
- Completion: _complete via ledger.complete_and_append (storage/postgres/ledger.py:94-120) — stage_run UPDATE + StageCompleted append atomic in ONE txn.
- Cancel: JobService.cancel (application/jobs.py:140-159) whole/partial; handler pre-check reads persisted store (jobs/hatchet.py:296-307); drain gate (jobs/drain.py:45-67).
- Quarantine: _quarantine (stage_execution.py:335-357) deterministic MalformedInputError -> quarantine sink, never retried.
- Recovery/crash-resume: _existing_run + _replayed_complete + committed_prior_refs (stage_execution.py:393-508) — re-claim keys, completed dedupe (replayed=True), crashed resume; cross-job replay emits replay-marked StageCompleted observation (P2-S11).
- Rerun: JobService.rerun_stage/rerun_source + InvalidationPlanner descendant-only; submit_workflow_runs threads selected_stages + per-stage rerun_causation.
- Job status: _derive_status (application/jobs.py:348-367) + PostgresJobRepository.stage_states (job_repository.py:137-182, _STATUS_RANK precedence) + expected_stages/execution_causation in job.request.

9-TASK HATCHET TRANSLATION: 9 stages, 11 dependency edges, 8 evidence classes; one workflow, 9 durable tasks, 1 WorkflowVersion; per-job state = 9 stage_run rows + job_run_audit (start/retry/fail/complete/cancel) + 9 StageCompleted semantic events (+ replay observations for observing jobs). Selective rerun: full 9-task run submitted; unselected tasks replay (executor dedup), selected get fresh keys via rerun_causation; rerun cost = all 9 callbacks re-dispatched (8 replay). Proof surface: engine-visible-proof.sh Check 2 asserts exact per-task parent graph (umd-ingest -> ... -> umd-current_search_projection).

MISSING IF HATCHET DISAPPEARS: engine-side DAG barrier (match conditions), worker assignment/lease/heartbeat, queue, scheduler-level retry re-dispatch, timeouts on stuck tasks, dashboard. Postgres side already owns: claim, idempotency, atomic completion, audit, quarantine, job status, drain, rerun planning. NOT owned by Postgres: dispatch/queue, DAG gating (dependents fail closed MissingRequiredEvidenceError, no retry), lease expiry (stuck claimed rows only resume when re-driven), no non-polling restart path (Task.md §23 restartable; DD prohibits second scheduler/polling — a PG re-driver would BE a scheduler).

HATCHET vs POSTGRES-QUEUE vs TEMPORAL: Hatchet adds the DAG barrier + durable dispatch that the requirement set (Task.md §§6,16,23,40.19-21,30) demands; Postgres queue would need a re-driver loop = second scheduler (prohibited by DD §Durable stage execution). Temporal (durable workflow replay, signals for cancel, child-workflow DAG) would satisfy the same requirements with a heavier server; UMD idempotency authority stays in Postgres either way ("engine idempotency is advisory"), so Temporal is a like-for-like scheduler swap, not an architectural change — but the pinned SDK/server pair, tenant/JWT, and proof surface are all Hatchet-specific.

Evidence: full file set read with line ranges; prior skills umd-hatchet-v1-scheduler-barrier + umd-hatchet-dependency-barrier + logs L11-L15. No decisions dir exists (artifacts/decisions absent) — no ADR work.

title: Ingestion command duplication, OCFL readiness gap, tx drift, authority ownership
body:
Four findings from read-only source audit (Task.md + DD + src):

(1) DUPLICATE INGESTION COMMAND PATH. `src/umd/application/ingestion.py:75-155` `IngestionCommandHandler.ingest` ("Versioned ingestion command path (P3-S4)") is invoked ONLY by tests — grep `IngestionCommandHandler` in src/ = 1 match (the definition). The live REST path `src/umd/api/routers/sources.py::_submit_source` (164-252) re-implements the identical command inline (put_immutable :185, find_source_by_sha512 :199, ensure_work/ensure_source :209-223, record_source_ingested :224, dispatch :240) and NEVER imports the handler. Behavioral divergence: app path calls add_membership(role="primary") (ingestion.py:128); REST path NEVER does → REST-ingested sources have NO source_membership rows (repositories.py:432-438; tables.py:193 unique(source,work,role)); nothing reads memberships at runtime (grep `.memberships(` src = 0 matches) so it is latent. Also diverged: job_id (app=uuid4 placeholder+no dispatch vs REST=`job-{source_id[:12]}`+real dispatch :239-240), idempotency key (app=user-supplied vs REST=uuid5(NAMESPACE_URL, f"ingest:{source_id}") :234), source_id format (str(uuid4()) vs hex), created_by. src/umd/ingestion/__init__.py is a scaffold placeholder. DD:50 assigns command handlers+transaction boundaries to `application`.

(2) OCFL BOOTSTRAP READINESS. Bootstrap works: SourceStore.create (storage/ocfl/store.py:116-154, flock+staging, idempotent) called by build_source_store (api/entrypoints.py:19-21) at API and worker start (cli.py:81); compose mounts ocfl-data:/data/ocfl for api (compose.yaml:87) and worker (:128), UMD_OCFL__ROOT=/data/ocfl (:24). BUT the only runtime check is bootstrap-time: deploy/startup.py:108-167 readiness_probe HAS an OCFL component (namaste + inventory), yet nothing wires it — docker-entrypoint.sh (16-25) runs only migrations; /v1/ready (api/routers/system.py:93-111) checks ONLY projection freshness; /v1/health (:86-90) = projections+scheduler. OCFL status invisible post-start; a degraded root is never surfaced.

(3) TRANSACTION DRIFT. Ingestion commits in >=4 separate transactions + 1 FS op (OCFL write, ensure_work tx, ensure_source tx, ledger append tx, dispatch tx). Drift windows: orphan OCFL object (benign), orphan work row, source-row-without-SourceIngested (silently invisible to Tier-0/1; only a client retry heals via sha512 dedup + uuid5 key — nothing reconciles), and ledger-ok-but-dispatch-failed → job marked FAILED (application/jobs.py:117-122) + user 500. TOCTOU: find_source_by_sha512 (repositories.py:396-405) then ensure_source (407-430) in separate txs, source.sha512 UNIQUE (tables.py:136) → concurrent identical uploads: second ensure_source raises IntegrityError → unhandled 500; ensure_source has NO on_conflict_do_nothing. Ledger already provides the fix: complete_and_append (ledger.py:94-120) + _append_all_events_on (122-213), docstring (:83-86) explicitly says side-effect anchors must use the same connection — ingestion doesn't. Evidence/segment rows are written by stage work in their OWN transactions (evidence.record repositories.py:229-290; segment put :54-76) BEFORE the StageCompleted complete_and_append (stage_execution.py:273-333); crash → re-run dedups via uq_evidence_identity (migrations 0003), but abandoned jobs leave orphan evidence rows.

(4) AUTHORITY OWNERSHIP. Documented: DD:45 "semantic ledger is the only semantic write authority"; DD:111-123 ownership invariants; app.py:272-273; system.py:147 capabilities semantic_authority=tier0-ledger; docs/consistency.md. Ledger append-only enforced by DB trigger (migrations 0001:34-50). Reality: evidence+segments are written DIRECTLY by stage work repositories (allowed by DD "stage artifact writer"/"command path" but no application command layer; executor is the de facto command); source/work rows are written by the ROUTER (api layer) not application; membership authority ambiguous (app path writes, REST doesn't, nothing reads). USER_OVERRIDE precedence per poison.py:96-108 + reducer (docs/consistency.md:104).

title: Semantic capability repairs — research findings (production text path, placeholders, typed surfaces)
body: Deep research for planning the semantic capability repairs. Key results: (1) production.py text path bypasses dispatch: _parsed_text (313-317) always normalize_txt(raw).text (UTF-8 errors="replace" — binary coercion for EPUB/PDF), _basic_segmentation (940-969) always segment_txt (segment_markdown/segment_epub exist but unused), _emit_low_level_text_evidence (394-422) hardcodes chapter/1 paths; _parser_for (319-324) is metric-only. (2) Deterministic analysis single-chapter: text_structural.py _locator_for hardcodes chapter=1; no scenes/utterances/presence/traits/emotions. (3) Placeholder semantic stages: _entity_resolution (1084-1111) one ALIAS canonical per source; _semantic_reconciliation (1129-1147) single RECONCILED_SOURCE assertion — no rich KG assertions. (4) Multi-edge: current_state single row per (entity_ref,predicate); alternatives replay-only; full history in semantic_assertion (append-only) — active multi-edge read side missing. (5) Existing typed surfaces suffice: EntityType/PREDICATE_VOCABULARY+EXTENDED_PREDICATES/register_predicate (no migration), SemanticAssertion provenance shape, commands (assert_semantic/override/lock/invalidate/entity_resolve), QueryService kinds incl UTTERANCE/SCENE/UNRESOLVED_ALIASES, SearchProjectionBuilder. (6) Evidence IDs random (repositories.py:248) — deterministic-ID gap. (7) No parity-oracle/Alexandria terms in repo — repair ledger is caller-supplied. (8) Fixtures single-chapter only; no public StageWork E2E over multi-chapter book. Full detail saved to .opencode/skills/umd-semantic-capability-repairs/SKILL.md.
